message.reasoning_content:
The user wants a full transcription of a two-page OIML Certificate of Conformity. This is a document they provided, so transcribing it is fine — it's a government/certificate document, and transcription of user-provided documents is a standard task. The IP reminder says quoting from a provided document is acceptable.

Let me transcribe both pages carefully.

Page 1:
- Header: Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt (bold, large)
- Braunschweig und Berlin (bold)
- Left: "Member State of OIML Germany"
- Center: German federal eagle logo (image) — I should note it as image text? The instruction says text embedded in images (logos...) must be transcribed too. The logo is the federal eagle — it contains no text. I could indicate [German federal eagle logo] — but they said don't annotate. Hmm. The logo is an image without text. I'll represent it minimally, perhaps as a description in brackets. Rules say text embedded in images must be transcribed — the eagle has no text. I'll include something like ![Federal eagle] but that might be annotation. Safer: include a bracketed placeholder like "[Image: German federal eagle]" — that's transcribing presence of image. Given ambiguity, I'll include a small note. Actually the instruction: "Text embedded in images (logos, stamps, accuracy-class markings, table scans, signatures) must be transcribed too." So only text embedded in images. The eagle has no text, so nothing to transcribe. But signatures on page 2 — they're handwritten signatures with no legible text. I'll not add annotation. But maybe minimal placeholders are acceptable. I'll include nothing for the eagle since no text.

- Right: "OIML Certificate N°" / "R60/2000-DE1-10.03"

There are signatures on page 2 presumably (above names) — signatures themselves are images without clear text; I won't transcribe anything. Actually maybe I should indicate them minimally. The rules say transcribe text embedded in images — signatures are listed as examples, but a signature contains a name... The names are printed below. The handwritten signatures aren't legible text. I'll not include placeholders to avoid annotation, but including a placeholder like "[signature]" could be considered annotation. Hmm. To be safe and faithful, I'll not add placeholders for wordless graphics. Actually, I think a minimal bracketed note for the logo and signatures helps fidelity but the user said "Do not summarize, translate, annotate, or omit anything." A bracketed [signature] is arguably an annotation. I'll omit since no text.
